newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Britain says is eager to invest more in Bangladesh.
newsitem.headline: Britain says is eager to invest more in Bangladesh.

text.p: Britain is aiming to invest more in Bangladesh's infrastructure in its efforts to support the country's development process, Sir Martin Laing, Chairman of British Overseas Trade Board said on Sunday.
"We are eager to invest more in infrastructure especially in Bangladesh's energy sector," he told Bangladeshi businessmen at ametting.

Laing arrived here on Sunday leading a six-member British business delegation on a three-day visit. It is taking place just after the visit of the British Prime Minister John Major earlier this month.
"We are particularly interested about Bangladesh as more than 300,000 of its citizen working in Britain are contributing enormously to the economy of Britain."
Laing said more than 45 British firms were operating in Bangladesh in a wide range of sectors and three more companies would join them later this year.
Britain's involvement is the second largest in Bangladesh with over $300 million of direct investment registered in the country.

He said Britain was convinced about Bangladesh's liberalised policies and incentives offered to the foreign investors. "They (British investors) believe there exists a congenial investment climate in Bangladesh under the new government," he said.
A.S.M. Quasem, president of the Dhaka Chamber of Commerce and Industry (DCCI), which organised the meeting, said that Britain was also the second largest export market of Bangladesh products.
Bangladesh's exports to Britain totalled $426.7 million in the 11 months to November, 1996 against imports worth $109 million from that country, according to official figures.

He said: "We want to see Britain as our development partner." He referred to Major's assurance to Bangladeshi businessmen saying Britain was keen to be Bangladesh's partner in trade, devlopment and investment.

During his visit Major witnessed a new $150 million investment contract signed by British Cairn Enery Plc with Bangladesh's state-owned Petrobangla. Cairn has already found huge gas reserves in the Bay of Bengal.
Quasem said Bangladesh could provide a useful low cost production base for foreign investors in several sectors like agro-based industry, textile, finished leather, ceramic and capital market.

He said Bangladesh had offered a package of incentives to attract foreign investment including repatriation of profit and capital and duty free imports of capital machinery for export-oriented industry.
